lines.text: Marian opens her eyes in her room.
She rushes out of the room and down the stairs.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Commander! Commander!
At the bottom is Doctor Maria, drinking with a rigid expression on her face.
For just a brief moment, Marian meets Doctor Maria's eyes, then runs again.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Where are you going?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: The Commander! I have to make sure he's all right!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... He's all right.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: His memories are intact too.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ...I-I have to see for myself!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Marian. Come here.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: We need to talk.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'm sorry, Doctor, but let me check on the Commander first...!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I told you No. 7 is fine!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Do you not trust me?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's... not that...! I just...!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Come here.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Now.
Marian slowly walks to Doctor Maria.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Sit.
Marian pulls out a chair and sits.
Doctor Maria empties the glass in front of her.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Have you lost your mind?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Going back the way you came? What were you thinking?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You're supposed to push forward toward the target location, not turn back.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You tried to get him treated? Did you lose your mind?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You could have exposed our location to the Raptures!
The anxious, frightened look in Marian's eyes suddenly turns cold.
She looks straight into Doctor Maria's vacant eyes and speaks.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Doctor.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: The transport ship wasn't there.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Yeah, the transport ship drops you off, and then comes back.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Of course, we've still lost dozens of them along the way.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: So coming back here was never an option for us?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... No, it wasn't.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You come back when you die, though. Why would you not use such an easy solution?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: When does this end, Doctor?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: That's a strange thing to ask all of a sudden.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'm worried it'll suddenly end one day without warning.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: That I'll die the same as always, like it's nothing,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: but then if that turns out to be the last time,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: if I don't actually come back...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: The thought paralyzes me with fear.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... That won't happen. So long as I'm here, nothing like that will ever—

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And what if something happens to you?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You could slip on the stairs... get food poisoning... get electrocuted by malfunctioning machinery... or there could be a fire...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Humans die so easily.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's almost hard to believe how easily they can die.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And you're human, Doctor.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Then that's where it ends.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: For you, and for me.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... And for everything we've gained up to now.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Honestly, Doctor, what I'm scared of isn't the idea of not coming back to life.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'm scared of all these memories disappearing.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: To have it all vanish in an instant... I don't even want to imagine it.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: What's gotten into you?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You becoming afraid of death is not something I really understand, if I'm being honest, but I can accept it.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: But now you're scared your memories will be erased?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: If I erase your memories, you won't even remember that I erased them.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: There's nothing to be afraid of.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: As always, you'll just keep on...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Keep on what?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Keep on dying and coming back to life?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: As if that's all I was born for... or, should I say, created for.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Am I supposed to just keep dying and coming back, regardless of my will?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Always possessed of the fear that there might not be a next time,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: doomed to repeat the process over and over?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Is that it for me?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: For the Nikke named Marian?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Is that to be my entire existence?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Doctor.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What do you see me as?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You're...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Is this because of No .7?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... You're avoiding my question.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You first. Is this because of No. 7?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Yes.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'm okay with not coming back.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'm okay with all my memories disappearing.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: If I die, then I'll be gone anyway,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: and if I lose my memories, it's like you said. I'll never even know I had them to begin with.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: But what about him?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What about the Commander?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What would he feel like, being on the transport ship we always rode together, without me there?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: How would he feel if he started a conversation with me like normal, only for me to act as if we'd never met?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It hurts just thinking about it.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Thinking of how sad he'd be... it makes me crazy.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What's even scarier, though,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: is thinking that the Commander could die, or lose his memories,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: and then I'd never see him again,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: or he'd stop being able to remember me.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: That's what scares me the most.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Do you love No. 7?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Yes. I love him.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... You're just confused.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: All those warm feelings you have for No. 7 are an illusion,

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: as is that longing you feel but can't quite define.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: See, the memories you have of that little boy are all...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I know. They're yours.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I was made from your memories.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I never led a human life, so I wouldn't have any childhood memories.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Those are your memories. I know that.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... You knew.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... How do you remember the Commander?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Exactly the same way as you do. That same feeling.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: He was a ray of sunshine.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Looking back now, he had a way of moving a girl's heart even at that age.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... I was born entirely according to my mother's meticulous plans.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I was the contingency in the event that something happened to her.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I was born through artificial insemination. I'm what they call a test-tube baby.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I don't know who my father is. My mother said she only received the sperm of the man she judged to be the finest candidate.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I was created completely out of necessity.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: A backup for my mother...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: And essentially a designer baby, made for the purpose of increasing NIMPH compatibility.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: It probably goes without saying, but I never actually met my mother. By the time I was born, she had already turned into what she is now.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: She became humanity's enemy. And her blood runs through my veins.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I had to somehow achieve something greater than her.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: That's what I was made for, after all.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: While I may have been created as a human with high NIMPH compatibility, actually proving it was agonizing.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: It wasn't the kind of pain a child could just endure.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Of course, the "distinguished" researchers at the time lied and told me there was a problem with my brain.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: But it was just a lot of pain.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: That boy was a huge comfort to me back then.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: He was the reason I was able to hold on.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: But that's all he was.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: The moment the NIMPH took, I threw myself into preparing the Silver Gun Squad, almost like I was possessed.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: This NIMPH in my head... Turns out it contains all of my mother's knowledge as-is.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: All these things I had to do and get ready came rushing into my mind like a flood.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: So I forgot about that boy.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: He became a vague memory, and it ended there.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: That's everything I think about No. 7.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: He was someone in passing who helped me forget about the pain I was going through at the time. Nothing more, nothing less.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... I see.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: It's a worthless memory to me.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You've taken it and treated it like it was fate or something,

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: but it's not even your memory.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: So those feelings you have right now are fake.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You're just confused.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... Did that memory really have no impact on your future?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Did it really mean nothing to you as you lived your life?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... Unfortunately, yeah.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Then I'll take it. That memory.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... What?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's my memory now.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: What are you talking about? You can't just take or discard whatever memories you...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Sure I can, because that's what I am.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Someone who can take or discard memories as needed.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: So when it comes to that memory, I'm taking it. It's mine.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's what gave me the strength to endure all of that hellish time I was alone.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Thanks to it, I was able to meet the Commander.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And thanks to him, I found a goal worth living for.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Now I am able to think about and get excited for what comes next.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You told me my memory would be a source of strength that carries me forward, didn't you?

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You were right.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: The memory of us meeting when "I" was young, and all the memories we've been making... They give me strength.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And because of that, I've decided to keep moving forward.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: So, Doctor.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: What I feel for him is real.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And it's all mine.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: It's not anything you made. It was born of "my" memories, and it's all mine.
Doctor Maria lifts her glass.
The alcohol is gone, with only water from melted ice left.
Still, she brings the glass to her lips.
The alcohol has left her system, but her vision is still blurred.
Through that haze,
she sees clear and resolute eyes looking straight back at her.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: are better than me.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You're much better than me.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: ... This time, we are going to make it to the target location.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And after we do, we'll move on to whatever is next.
Marian rises from her seat.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Marian.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: No. 7 won't last long.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: He's a human who gets revived and keeps his memories after dying. There's no way he's normal.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: So don't get too...

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: In that case,

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: I'll just have to love him as much as I can, so that I don't have any regrets.
Marian breaks into a run.
Doctor Maria can't take her eyes off her.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: *Huff... huff...!*
Marian runs.
She practically leaps down the stairs.
She doesn't need the "enhancement procedure." Right now, even that feels like it would take too much time away from them.
The transport ship she's seen hundreds of times before comes into view.
Marian hits the button to open the ramp door.
She stamps her feet impatiently as the ramp door slowly lowers.
The ramp door finally opens completely, and Marian sprints in.
And there, in that same spot, with that same expression:
Hi, Marian.
She sees the person she loves, offering the same warm greeting as always.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: Commander...!
Marian runs to the Commander.
He stands up and opens both arms.
They hold each other tight.

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: You came back...! Thank goodness...!

lines.speaker: marian
lines.text: And you didn't forget me...! I'm so glad...!
I'm glad you came back too, Marian.
And I'm really happy you didn't forget me.
